import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    # Create a dummy dataframe for environments where the file doesn't exist
    data = {
        'brand': np.random.choice(['Canon', 'Nikon', 'Sony', 'Fuji', 'Leica', 'Pentax'], 1000),
        'model_year': np.random.randint(2005, 2024, 1000),
        'megapixels': np.random.uniform(10, 60, 1000),
        'max_iso': np.random.choice([12800, 25600, 51200, 102400, 204800], 1000),
        'weight_grams': np.random.randint(200, 1500, 1000),
        'price_usd': np.random.lognormal(mean=7.5, sigma=0.8, size=1000),
        'sensor_type': np.random.choice(['Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Micro 4/3'], 1000),
        'has_video_4k': np.random.randint(0, 2, 1000),
        'lens_mount': ['E', 'EF', 'F', 'MFT', 'X'][i % 5] for i in range(1000),
        'body_type': ['DSLR', 'Mirrorless', 'Compact'][i % 3] for i in range(1000)
    }
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)
    df.loc[df['sensor_type'] == 'Full Frame', 'price_usd'] *= 1.8
    df.loc[df['sensor_type'] == 'Full Frame', 'megapixels'] += 10
    df.loc[df['has_video_4k'] == 1, 'price_usd'] *= 1.3

# Data cleaning and preparation
df['price_usd'] = df['price_usd'].clip(upper=8000) # Cap price for better visualization
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K', 1: 'Has 4K'})
df_filtered = df[df['model_year'] >= 2010].copy()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatterplot
# This plot shows the relationship between price and megapixels,
# while encoding sensor type as color, 4K capability as marker style,
# and max ISO as the size of the points.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='has_video_4k_label',
    size='max_iso',
    sizes=(30, 300),
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Improve labels and title for clarity
plt.title('Camera Market Landscape (2010-Present): Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Format y-axis to display as currency
formatter = plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${int(x):,}')
plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.gca().tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=10)


# Adjust legend
handles, labels = scatter_plot.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually reorder and title legend sections for better readability
sensor_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label in ['sensor_type', 'Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Micro 4/3']]
video_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label in ['has_video_4k_label', 'Has 4K', 'No 4K']]
iso_idx = [i for i, label in enumerate(labels) if label in ['max_iso', '12800', '25600', '51200', '102400', '204800']]

# Combine ordered handles and labels
new_handles = [handles[i] for i in sensor_idx + video_idx + iso_idx]
new_labels = [labels[i] for i in sensor_idx + video_idx + iso_idx]

# Place legend outside the plot
plt.legend(
    new_handles,
    new_labels,
    title='Features',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=10,
    title_fontsize=12,
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True
)

# Add a grid for easier reading
plt.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Final adjustment to layout
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
